answer: Persistent resource trail. Each agent identity accrues a non-transferable history of scarce physical inputs it consumed, logged as slow-moving reserves: like a glacier, the record accumulates and cannot be reset or copied without matching consumption. A new identity starts empty and must draw fresh river allocations under a per-source quota, while shared provenance of timber deliveries is cross-checked against the same trail. Duplicates fragment these reserves, and each clone pays full quota consumption again, making duplication visibly expensive and self-revealing.
